## Today in Energy [More Today in Energy](https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/ "More Today in Energy")

Posted May 20, 2026

### [Coal remains competitive for power generation in the central United States ›](https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=67705)


**Data source:** U.S. Energy Information Administration, based on data from S&P Global Market Intelligence  
**Note:** The specifics of the calculation methodology are detailed in our [2017 Today in Energy article](https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=33312), with minor adjustments to heat rates and heat contents used. The heat rate used for the dark spread was 10,579 British thermal units per kilowatthour (Btu/kWh) while the heat rate for the spark spread was 8,365 Btu/kWh.

* * *

In the first four months of 2026, electricity, natural gas, and coal prices suggested continued favorable economics for coal generation in MISO. The [dark spread](https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=10051) of coal, the difference between the fuel costs for coal-fired generation and the wholesale electricity price, in the Midcontinent Independent System Operator (MISO) region outpaced a similar measure of revenue relative to fuel costs for natural gas-fired generators known as the [spark spread](https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=9911).

[More ›](https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=67705 "More")

* * *

### Previously in Today in Energy

*   [Data center server energy use grows across the commercial building stock](https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=67704)
*   [U.S. industrial natural gas consumption expected to hit records in 2026 and 2027](https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=67686)
*   [Electricity generation from solar could exceed coal in ERCOT for the first time in 2026](https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=67685)
*   [More](https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/ "More Today in Energy")
